dedupe_keys.name: may 2016 wood buffalo fort mcmurray wildfire provincial post incident assessment of evacuation and support

description: This case study is the Government of Alberta's post-incident assessment of the May 2016 Wood Buffalo wildfire, also called the Horse River fire, which forced the evacuation of Fort McMurray. It was prepared by KPMG for the Alberta Emergency Management Agency and published in May 2017 as a 167-page report, free to download online as a PDF from the Alberta open government portal. The assessment drew on the knowledge of those involved and affected and focuses on the province's support to stakeholders, emergency social services and the community evacuations, including the delegation of authority between the province and the regional municipality. The fire was first seen on 1 May about 7 kilometres from the urban area and reached the community on 3 May; almost 88,000 people were evacuated in a very short time, 589,000 hectares burned over five weeks and 1,958 structures were lost or damaged, and the total financial and economic impact was estimated at almost 8.9 billion dollars. Coverage is the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo. The portal lists no licence. Caveats: the report reviews provincial roles only, and a separate review covered wildfire management. It makes recommendations on prevention, preparedness, evacuation planning, staging of resources and support to evacuees. Simulation uses: an observed case for wildfire evacuation, shelter and reception models. Related records: the Camp Fire notification and evacuation case (case_study-camp-fire-2018-notification-evacuation) is a comparable wildland-urban interface evacuation.
